description: The NWS Rothfusz regression for heat index with both low-humidity and high-humidity adjustments, plus danger-level bands.

faqs.a: The Rothfusz regression, published by the US National Weather Service, combines air temperature (°F) and relative humidity (%) into one 'feels like' number. Low-humidity (≤13%) and high-humidity (>85%) adjustments from the NWS are applied.
faqs.q: What is the heat index formula?

faqs.a: 80–90°F caution, 91–103°F extreme caution, 104–124°F danger, 125°F+ extreme danger. The tool labels your result automatically.
faqs.q: What are the heat danger levels?

faqs.a: Shade can make it feel up to 15°F cooler, while full sun can add up to 15°F to the heat index value.
faqs.q: Does shade change the heat index?

howto: Read the heat index and its danger-level band.
